chapter: Favorite bands, advice and family reflections
title: The family was never hungry
summary: Eutris says the family was better off than poor whites, farming a big plantation with a spring.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, we never went hungry. We were never hungry and ... I have seen the white people come to my parents to even borrow food ... but they would borrow something from my family.
I don't know. I couldn't say. But, we seemed to be more well off than they were.
Would you say that you were better off than the average?
You said poor white but if there was a middle class, were you on a par with middle class white?
I would say the middle class. There wasn't any wealthy people because the town was too small.

But if you owned extensive land and you had sharecroppers on the land then all of the white people -- were white people sharecroppers also on white property or on black property. Was there such a thing as a white sharecropper?

At first, my father was a sharecropper. But, he moved from that place ... where we were all born on the railroad, do you remember? But, he moved to another big place (owned by ________) where we had fruit, all kinds of fruit and a vegetable garden and the land, and the lots and everything where you send the cows to pasture, people used to come there, young people to play ball in the summertime. It was big enough to have picnics and all. And, do you remember that?
And that's where my sisters had taught school. It was a big plantation. Go swimming and everything.
People in the city would have (Football?) teams one in the city and one out in the country. They would come out like on weekends and play.
And they still have two years ago those ... you know when we went home to bury my sister. The place is run down but they still have the water spring. ...
